title: Reduce session fanout and slim KV cache index to cut memory and scheduler contention
creator: Aisha Mehta
description: This ticket consolidates duplicate session-level fanout paths and replaces the heavy per-session KV index with a compact global index. The goal is to reduce memory pressure from in-memory KV entries, lower scheduler mutex contention during batching, and simplify eviction semantics for smoother latency under bursty load. This touches continuous batching, KV cache book-keeping, and the ingress scheduler's lease/tick path.
acceptance_criteria: Memory used by KV index reduced by >=25% for 1M active keys in internal memsim
P50 generation latency improves or remains within 3% of baseline under 2k qps steady-state
No increase in tail latency (P99) beyond 5% when running mixed short/long sequence workloads
Eviction correctness: no KV lookup misses observed in end-to-end smoke tests and canary traffic
All existing unit/integration tests pass; new tests cover compact-index recovery and epoch rollover
technical_notes: Problem: sessions create duplicated lightweight indices for hot prefixes which causes memory duplication and frequent small locks on the scheduler path.
Design: introduce a compact global index (compact-index) sharded by high bits of session-id; store lightweight pointers from session metadata instead of full per-session maps.

Scheduler changes: move from fine-grained per-session mutex in the admission path to epoch-based sampling + lock-free readpath for common case; write-path uses a short critical section to update tombstones.
KV cache changes: unify eviction queues into a two-tier LRU where hot keys are promoted to an in-memory hotset; background compactor coalesces tombstones and reclaims memory asynchronously.

Dependency upgrades: bump rocksdb -> 7.4.1 (for 'IngestExternalFile' performance fixes) and bump tokio -> 1.30 to get improved timer wheel behavior; both upgrades included in separate dependency PRs and listed as dependencies below.

Trade-offs: compact-index increases read indirection (one extra pointer chase) but reduces memory and lock contention. We expect small p50 regressions for some synthetic microbenchmarks; end-to-end tests should show net improvement due to less GC/allocator pressure.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged at startup; rollout canary to 5% then 25% then 100% with automatic rollback on P99 regressions or increased errors. Fallback path keeps legacy per-session index and can be toggled without restart in early experiments.
Observability: new metrics kvcache.compact_index_hits, kvcache.indirections, scheduler.epoch_ticks, and kvcache.compactor_cycles added. Add trace spans for 'compact-lookup' in request traces.
steps: Spike: microbenchmark compact-index vs per-session map with realistic key distributions (done)
Implement compact-index sharded data structure and session pointer plumbing
Refactor scheduler admission path to use epoch-readpath and short-lived write locks
Implement background compactor and eviction two-tier logic
Add unit/integration tests and fault-injection harness for tombstone recovery
Create dependency upgrade PRs for RocksDB and Tokio and coordinate CI matrix
Run canary rollout with 5% traffic; monitor metrics and dashboard
Iterate on thresholds and finalize documentation and runbook
progress_updates: 2026-02-19: Spike completed — synthetic memsim shows ~33% index memory reduction with compact-index prototype (Aisha).

2026-03-02: Implemented prototype of compact-index and session pointer refs; basic unit tests passing. Found contention hotspot in allocator — flagged for allocator tuning. (Luca)
2026-03-07: Opened dependency PRs: rocksdb upgrade PR (#1285) and tokio upgrade PR (#1286). CI green on linux-amd64; flaky test on mac-arm tracked in ENG-482900 (dependency test flake).
2026-03-09: End-to-end memsim against mixed workloads shows p50 -7% and p99 +2% with 30% memory reduction after compaction step. Preparing canary plan.
notes_for_reviewers: Please focus on the compactor correctness and recovery paths — tombstone retention semantics are subtle.
Benchmarks attached use memsim artifacts under /tmp/memsim/compact-index and are reproducible with tools/run_memsim.sh.
If approving the RocksDB and Tokio upgrades, coordinate with infra on rolling restart windows for Dedicated clusters.
